message.reasoning:
Ready to play Monopoly.

I'm on Boardwalk with $756 and a utility monopoly. I'm missing New York Avenue to complete the orange group and Oriental/Connecticut to complete the light purple group. I also need to check if p2 has a yellow monopoly.

p2 holds Ventnor, Pacific, and Mediterranean. p3 owns all four railroads plus St. Charles and Illinois but has only $255 cash. p4 just bought Boardwalk and currently owns Marvin Gardens, North Carolina, and Boardwalk.

New York Avenue is still unowned and the key to completing the orange group. I'll skip mortgaging or selling utilities since cash is healthy. I won't re-offer the Reading trade to p3 immediately. Building isn't possible yet. Now considering a trade with p4.

p4 lacks any missing pieces I need for a monopoly. Illinois is owned by p3, so that trade path is blocked. St. Charles is also not useful right now. I'm now considering whether to propose a different offer to p3.

I won't overpay for Illinois. I'm now looking at p2, who has $1646 and wants color sets, but I don't have anything that would complete one of theirs. I'm also checking whether any trade could help me directly.

I'll skip trading this turn. Repeated offers would annoy other players and lack a clear positive value. I won't help p4 complete their dark blue set either, since Park Place is still unowned.

I'm now reconsidering a trade with p3. Indiana plus cash could be offered for Illinois, giving me two reds and allowing me to complete the set when Kentucky is auctioned. I rejected the idea of trading utilities since they generate rent.

I'm now weighing whether p3 would sell Illinois for cash. They paid $240 for it and are cash-poor, but they might not want to help me complete a red monopoly.

p3 explicitly wants to keep their rail network intact. I'm now considering offering $300–$350 cash for Illinois, which would leave me with enough money to buy New York Avenue and still provide a strong red monopoly once Kentucky is auctioned.

I'm now uncertain about the $350 Illinois offer. Two reds would be speculative if another player buys Kentucky first. I can afford New York Avenue after that spend, but not both properties immediately.

I'll end the turn. A $300–$350 Illinois offer would leave me too exposed to rail and rent hits, so I'm preserving cash for New York Avenue and the orange plan.

I'm drafting a short public message that doesn't reveal my strategy. I briefly considered selling Vermont Avenue to p4 for a large cash sum, hoping to prevent them from buying Park Place, but rejected the idea.
